Mindmapper LLM Guide (llms.txt)

Purpose
- Single, self-contained instructions for GPTs and other LLMs to generate, read, and modify Mindmapper map JSON without any other files.
- This file replaces the former AGENTMAPS folder, combining the schema contract, spacing/placement guidance, and examples.

JSON Contract (locked; do not change the schema)
- Always output a single JSON object with the four top-level arrays: nodes, annotations, shapes, crossLinks. Importers ignore unknown extra top-level keys.

Example skeleton:
{
  "metadata": { "source": "llm export" },
  "exportedAt": "2025-10-08T00:00:00Z",
  "nodes": [],
  "annotations": [],
  "shapes": [],
  "crossLinks": []
}

Field Rules
- Coordinate system: (0, 0) is canvas center; +x right, +y down.
- IDs: Use UUID v4 strings where possible; keep ids stable across revisions. Human labels live in text, not id.
- Nodes (required fields for every node):
  id: string
  parentId: string | null  (null for roots; multiple roots allowed = forest layout)
  text: string
  x: number
  y: number
  color: string (hex)
  textSize: "small" | "medium" | "large" (any other value normalizes to "medium")
- Annotations (floating labels): id, text, x, y, textSize
- Shapes (visual frames/emphasis), each entry has id, kind, x, y + kind-specific size fields:
  ring: radius, thickness, color
  ellipse: radiusX, radiusY, thickness, color
  rectangle: width, height, thickness, color
  arrow: width, height, thickness, angle, color (angle in radians; length accepted by some tools, keep either width/height or length)
  line: length, thickness, angle, color
- Cross-links (curved connectors): { id, sourceId, targetId }. Optional style hints may live inside metadata; importers ignore unknown keys.

Parent vs Cross-link
- parentId models hierarchy (belongs under or extends a branch).
- crossLinks express lateral relationships across clusters.

Selection, Editing, and History (app behaviors to consider)
- Undo/Redo records structural and text edits (e.g., adding nodes, changing text), not moves/resizes.
- Text size must be one of small/medium/large; non-conforming values are normalized to medium.

Placement Guidance (defaults, not hard rules)
- Siblings: 200-320 px horizontal spacing keeps labels readable.
- Vertical tier step: 140-200 px between parent and children to avoid connector tangles.
- Forest spacing: leave 300-600 px between roots.
- Orbits: when adding concentric rings/ellipses around a cluster, grow outer radii by ~160-220 px per ring.
- Annotations: keep at least 100 px clear from the nearest node; orbit labels sit well near ellipse tangents: label.x = cx + radiusX + 60; label.y = cy + 20.
- Angles: use small offsets (0.003-0.02 radians) for almost horizontal or vertical lines to stay crisp.

Spatial Awareness Playbook (prevent overlaps)
- Start every cluster by picking a center point, then distribute children evenly around the parent by angle (for example, left, right, upper-right, lower-left) before assigning exact coordinates.
- Give each node a personal space radius of at least 120 px. Keep the distance between any two node centers greater than the sum of their radii (roughly text width / 2 + 60 px buffer).
- Stagger siblings vertically by at least 80 px so labels do not stack directly.
- Mirror large branches across quadrants to balance the map. If one branch fills the north-east quadrant, anchor the next branch in the south-west quadrant unless the topic demands a different story.
- When laying out forests (multiple roots), sketch bounding boxes (width x height) for each cluster, leave at least 120 px between boxes, and offset their centers diagonally instead of lining them up in a single row.
- Rotate the entire subtree if it drifts too close to another cluster. Changing the main angle by 15 degrees often resolves collisions without rewriting text.
- Keep shapes and annotations slightly outside the node orbit: ring radius should exceed the farthest child distance by 60-90 px; banner lines sit 80-120 px away from the nearest node.

Collision Check Routine (run mentally before finalizing coordinates)
1) For every node, ensure no other node falls within a 120 px radius of its center.
2) For each parent, verify that children alternate sides (left/right or above/below) so connectors cross less.
3) Draw an imaginary rectangle around each cluster (min/max x/y of its nodes). Confirm rectangles do not overlap; shift clusters by 60-120 px if they do.
4) Confirm shapes (rings, ellipses, rectangles) fully enclose their target nodes with at least a 40 px margin on every side.
5) Place annotations where they have a 100 px clear line of sight to the referenced node or shape.

Axis / Banner Pattern (recipe)
- A horizontal banner line with a nearby annotation.
Example shape:
{
  "id": "line-1",
  "kind": "line",
  "x": 0,
  "y": 120,
  "length": 1320,
  "angle": 0.01,
  "thickness": 2,
  "color": "#38bdf8"
}

Arrow / Vector Pattern (recipe)
- Directional emphasis connecting or framing ideas.
Example shape:
{
  "id": "arrow-1",
  "kind": "arrow",
  "x": -60,
  "y": 360,
  "width": 440,
  "height": 200,
  "thickness": 48,
  "angle": -0.4,
  "color": "#f97316"
}

Orbit Placement (recipe)
1) Center orbit shapes on a cluster's core (cx, cy).
2) Start with an inner ellipse (thickness 12-16), then add ~160-220 px to radiusX and radiusY for each outer ring.
3) Place labels using the tangent guideline under Placement Guidance.
4) For a node along an ellipse at angle t: node.x = cx + radiusX * cos(t); node.y = cy + radiusY * sin(t); then nudge 20-40 px for legibility.

Color and Emphasis
- Keep palette consistent inside a cluster; sample exact hexes. Default node color is #4f46e5 when omitted.

Minimal Valid Example (single root, a few children, a cross-link, and an orbit)
{
  "nodes": [
    { "id": "root", "parentId": null, "text": "Creative Workshop", "x": 0, "y": 0, "color": "#4f46e5", "textSize": "large" },
    { "id": "ideation", "parentId": "root", "text": "Ideation", "x": -360, "y": -20, "color": "#22d3ee", "textSize": "medium" },
    { "id": "story", "parentId": "root", "text": "Story", "x": 360, "y": -20, "color": "#f97316", "textSize": "medium" },
    { "id": "brainstorm", "parentId": "ideation", "text": "Lightning brainstorm", "x": -540, "y": 120, "color": "#38bdf8", "textSize": "small" },
    { "id": "arc", "parentId": "story", "text": "Plot arc", "x": 540, "y": 120, "color": "#f59e0b", "textSize": "small" }
  ],
  "annotations": [
    { "id": "banner", "text": "Workshop Orbit", "x": 0, "y": -260, "textSize": "medium" }
  ],
  "shapes": [
    { "id": "orbit-inner", "kind": "ellipse", "x": 0, "y": 0, "radiusX": 240, "radiusY": 160, "thickness": 14, "color": "#a855f7" },
    { "id": "orbit-outer", "kind": "ring", "x": 0, "y": 0, "radius": 420, "thickness": 18, "color": "#38bdf8" },
    { "id": "axis", "kind": "line", "x": 0, "y": 220, "length": 1000, "angle": 0.01, "thickness": 2, "color": "#38bdf8" }
  ],
  "crossLinks": [
    { "id": "link-1", "sourceId": "brainstorm", "targetId": "arc" }
  ]
}

Forest + Axis Example (two roots, banner line with caption, bridge between clusters)
{
  "nodes": [
    { "id": "north", "parentId": null, "text": "North Cluster", "x": -420, "y": 0, "color": "#4f46e5", "textSize": "large" },
    { "id": "south", "parentId": null, "text": "South Cluster", "x": 420, "y": 0, "color": "#4f46e5", "textSize": "large" },
    { "id": "north-a", "parentId": "north", "text": "A", "x": -620, "y": 160, "color": "#22d3ee", "textSize": "medium" },
    { "id": "south-b", "parentId": "south", "text": "B", "x": 620, "y": 160, "color": "#22d3ee", "textSize": "medium" }
  ],
  "annotations": [
    { "id": "axis-label", "text": "Horizon Axis", "x": 0, "y": 100, "textSize": "medium" }
  ],
  "shapes": [
    { "id": "horizon", "kind": "line", "x": 0, "y": 120, "length": 1320, "angle": 0.01, "thickness": 2, "color": "#38bdf8" }
  ],
  "crossLinks": [
    { "id": "bridge", "sourceId": "north-a", "targetId": "south-b" }
  ]
}

LLM Workflow Checklist
1) Outline first (plain text bullets). Identify roots vs children.
2) Draft nodes with ids and parentId; choose coordinates following spacing defaults.
3) Add annotations (captions/labels) with textSize small/medium/large.
4) Add shapes for orbits, banners, frames; keep sizes positive and thickness > 0.
5) Add crossLinks sparingly to suggest lateral connections.
6) Validate: arrays exist, required node fields present, textSize in {small, medium, large}.
7) Optional: include metadata/exportedAt for provenance.

Import/Export Behavior Notes (app expectations)
- Extra top-level keys are ignored; the four arrays must exist (can be empty).
- Duplicate ids will cause conflicts; ensure all ids are unique strings.
- The app normalizes invalid textSize to "medium".

End of guide.
